chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the killing of the tortoise and the quail: is it permissible to eat from it? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.قَتْلِ: killing (specifically by striking or throwing in this context)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat tortoise and quail if they are killed by striking them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the ruling on hunting by specifying that striking stones (*al-hajar*) and sling-stones (*al-bundiq*) does not constitute valid slaughter (*dhikr*), rendering the meat impermissible. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that for wild game to be halal, the act of killing must be accompanied by the invocation of God's name, distinguishing it from mere physical impact or blunt force trauma.
